skill.name: psql
skill.description: Run PostgreSQL queries, psql meta-commands, and SQL files from an AI-assisted CLI workflow.
skill.summary: Use psql from an AI assistant to inspect schemas, run queries, and execute SQL files.
skill.author: Bind

security_audit.summary: The high static score is partly inflated by Markdown backtick false positives, but the skill still exposes real risk. It intentionally runs psql commands, accepts arbitrary SQL or SQL files, and relies on .env or exported database credentials, so publication should require strong safeguards and clear warnings.

remediation.issue: Unrestricted SQL and psql meta-command execution
remediation.suggestion: Default to read-only connections where possible and require explicit confirmation before any non-SELECT query, meta-command, migration, or seed action.

remediation.issue: Database credentials are loaded from .env or exported environment variables
remediation.suggestion: Document least-privilege database users, avoid storing production passwords in project files, and redact credential values from all logs and outputs.

remediation.issue: SQL file execution can run local files supplied by the caller
remediation.suggestion: Restrict --file to approved project directories and show the target path before execution.

remediation.issue: Query results may contain sensitive application data
remediation.suggestion: Add guidance to limit result sizes, avoid broad user-data queries, and prefer aggregate or schema-only queries when debugging.

content.user_title: Run PostgreSQL Queries from AI Workflows
content.value_statement: Teams need a direct way to inspect PostgreSQL data while working with an AI assistant. This skill documents a psql CLI workflow for queries, schema checks, and SQL file execution.
actual_capabilities: Runs inline SQL queries through a documented psql command wrapper.
Runs psql meta-commands for tables, indexes, databases, and table details.
Executes SQL files for migrations or seed data workflows.
Supports tuple-only output for easier downstream parsing.
Supports a configurable timeout for longer database queries.
Can wrap command output in JSON for programmatic handling.
limitations: Requires both Bun and the psql client to be installed before use.
Requires PostgreSQL connection variables in the environment or a project .env file.
Runs each query as a separate psql invocation with no persistent session.
Does not document built-in read-only enforcement for dangerous SQL operations.

use_cases.title: Inspect application schemas
use_cases.description: List tables, describe table columns, and review indexes during development or debugging.

use_cases.title: Check operational database state
use_cases.description: Run aggregate queries, review active connections, and inspect table sizes from the terminal.

use_cases.title: Run controlled SQL files
use_cases.description: Execute migration or seed files in environments where credentials and approvals are already managed.

prompt_templates.title: List tables
prompt_templates.prompt: Use the psql skill to list the tables in the current PostgreSQL database.

prompt_templates.title: Describe a table
prompt_templates.prompt: Use the psql skill to describe the users table and show its columns, indexes, and constraints.

prompt_templates.title: Summarize recent activity
prompt_templates.prompt: Use the psql skill to count recent orders by status for the last day. Keep the result limited and do not change data.

prompt_templates.title: Review a migration file
prompt_templates.prompt: Use the psql skill to run the approved migration file after confirming the target database and showing the file path.

output_examples.input: List the tables in this database.
output_examples.output: The assistant runs the table listing command and leaves the psql table output visible in the terminal.

output_examples.input: Show the shape of the users table.
output_examples.output: The assistant runs a table description command and reports the columns, indexes, and constraints it observes.

output_examples.input: Check whether there are active database connections.
output_examples.output: The assistant runs a small administrative query and returns the active connection count.

best_practices: Use least-privilege database credentials, preferably read-only for inspection tasks.
Confirm the target database before running migrations, seed files, or broad data queries.
Limit result sizes and prefer aggregate queries when sensitive user data may be present.
anti_patterns: Do not use production administrator credentials for routine schema inspection.
Do not run unreviewed SQL files through the skill.
Do not ask the assistant to dump full tables that may contain private data.

faq.question: Does this skill require PostgreSQL to be installed?
faq.answer: Yes. The documented workflow requires the psql client and Bun runtime.

faq.question: Where does it get database credentials?
faq.answer: It expects PostgreSQL connection variables from the environment or a project .env file.

faq.question: Can it run psql meta-commands?
faq.answer: Yes. The documentation includes examples for table lists, table descriptions, indexes, and database lists.

faq.question: Can it execute SQL files?
faq.answer: Yes. The skill documents a --file option for migration and seed file execution.

faq.question: Does it keep a persistent database connection?
faq.answer: No. The documentation states that each query runs as a separate psql invocation.

faq.question: Is it safe for production databases?
faq.answer: Use caution. Production use should require least-privilege credentials, query review, and confirmation for state-changing operations.
